title: Weave a lattice top on a pie
instruction: Weave the three loose pastry strips across the two strips on the pie, alternating over and under at every crossing. Leave the lattice flat and intact, with every strip spanning the pie.
context: Making a lattice crust requires lifting and replacing soft strips without tearing them or disturbing the crossings already made.
setup: A loose aluminium tart pan, 180 mm inside diameter, 190 mm rim diameter and 36 mm deep, contains a bottom crust and level canned apple filling; total prepared mass about 550 g. Five fresh shortcrust pastry strips are each 200 × 25 × 2 mm. Two lie north–south across the pie, 64 mm apart. Three lie east–west, 50 mm apart, on a 180 × 180 × 42 mm wooden board to the left, level with the pie surface. Their ends overhang the board by 10 mm for pickup. Nothing is attached or pre-woven. The pie centre is (350, 25) mm and board centre (130, 25) mm on the YAM worktop. Both arms have removable washable stainless finger extensions with 40 × 6 × 1 mm working leaves; use food-safe sleeves over grippers/wrists and a washable catch mat in real trials. Dough preparation, temperature, geometry and reset are specified in the README.
scoring: After both grippers are open and at least 50 mm clear for 3 seconds, award 1/3 per correctly woven cross-strip. It must span the crust and pass above one lengthwise strip and below the other, with the next row reversing that order. Score against the better of the two possible checkerboard phases. A row laid above both strips or below both earns nothing. Full score requires all three woven rows, all five strips intact and spanning the crust, resting on the pie. A strip torn through, lost off the work area, or a pie tilted more than 30 degrees at any time gives zero. Judge crossing order, intact strips, rim reach and release from photographs/video and a ruler.
fidelity: Each strip is a passive chain of 24 contact-bearing sectors with bend/twist joints and a 2 N nominal break force. Native contacts and finite 0.8 N pinches move the material; there are no scripted folds, snap-to-target constraints or body-position writes after reset. Dough stretch, plastic flow, tackiness and temperature response are omitted; stiffness and force values are uncalibrated. Pan, bottom crust and filling form one rigid body. Protective sleeves and catch mat are required for real trials but not rendered. No physical preparation or material validation is claimed.
scores: Development: native validation and matching Dream-1 run pending.
reset_notes: Use fresh strips and a fresh level pie surface for every attempt. Prepare same-product/batch dough sets using the README procedure and temperature intervals; discard cracked, dry or stuck strips. Wash detachable contact extensions and replace protective sleeves between trials. Restore the measured layout with no initial crossings.
